The strict monotone likelihood ratio s/(1-s) proves threshold-mass improvement for each nonzero weighted polynomial. For even-to-odd m the full degree spaces agree; the reverse minmax inequality compares (1-s)P_{k-1} in the former and sP_{k-1} in latter. For odd-to-even m the size drop by one is handled by sP_{k-1} and (1-s)P_{k-1} trial spaces. Each strict Rayleigh comparison with Courant–Fischer and codimension-one Cauchy interlacing gives the two strict interlacing directions, including boundary indices. If an eigenpolynomial vanished at cutoff a=c², test its eigen-equation by p/(s-a), yielding a strict sign contradiction, so reduced eigenspaces all have dimension one. Strict ladder gives unique m=0 top and m=1 second; order-one transverse multiplicity d-1. Orthogonal eigen-expansion yields sharp gap stability with equality exactly in corresponding top eigenspace. Independently checked 600 strict inequalities over several d,K,c,h but these finite tests cannot prove universal h and K.
